papers.title: Peripartum Cardiomyopathy Genetic Screening Protocol and Registry: The PERCVD Trial in the Gulf South.
papers.abstract: Peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) is a pregnancy-associated form of systolic heart failure with high prevalence and mortality worldwide. It occurs in 1:1800 to 1:3500 births in the United States and disproportionately affects women in the Gulf South. Louisiana has the highest maternal mortality rate in the United States, yet no prospective registry exists to investigate the genetic basis of perinatal cardiovascular disorders, creating an urgent need for genetic assessment.
papers.summary: This paper describes the design of the PERCVD trial, a prospective genetic screening protocol and registry for peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) in the Gulf South, a region with disproportionately high maternal mortality. The registry aims to investigate the genetic basis of perinatal cardiovascular disorders, addressing a gap where no such prospective resource currently exists.

papers.title: Association of PRKCB Polymorphisms with Non-syndromic Orofacial Cleft among a Chinese Population.
papers.abstract: To investigate the association of PRKCB polymorphisms with non-syndromic orofacial cleft (NSOC) among a Chinese population.
papers.journal: The Chinese journal of dental research
papers.summary: This study investigates whether genetic variants in the PRKCB gene are associated with non-syndromic orofacial cleft (NSOC) in a Chinese population. It likely uses a case-control design to compare genotype frequencies between affected individuals and controls. The findings may identify PRKCB as a potential susceptibility locus for this common birth defect.

papers.title: Bridging BET bromodomain and immune checkpoint inhibitors through generative bioorganic frameworks for next-generation cancer immunotherapy.
papers.abstract: Bromodomain and extraterminal domain (BET) proteins are epigenetic readers that couple chromatin acetylation to oncogenic and immune-regulatory gene transcription, making them attractive targets for combination with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in precision oncology. This review synthesizes current mechanistic, medicinal-chemistry, and translational evidence on BET-ICI combination strategies. We describe how BET blockade reshapes tumor chromatin architecture, suppresses PD-L1 expression, and enhances antigen presentation, thereby increasing tumor susceptibility to immune-mediated attack
papers.summary: This review synthesizes mechanistic, medicinal-chemistry, and translational evidence on combining BET bromodomain inhibitors with immune checkpoint inhibitors for cancer therapy. It describes how BET blockade reshapes tumor chromatin architecture, suppresses PD-L1 expression, and enhances antigen presentation, thereby increasing tumor susceptibility to immune-mediated attack. The authors propose generative bioorganic frameworks to guide the design of next-generation BET-ICI combination strategies.

papers.title: Predicting Oncogenic Mutants of Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor in Lung Cancer by Molecular Dynamics Simulation with Machine Learning.
papers.abstract: The epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) is a frequently mutated protein kinase found in patients suffering from non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Although therapeutic drugs targeting EGFR are available, not all patients respond to these drugs, and it is not yet known whether some clinically detected mutations are actionable. Although the oncogenicity of some mutants is well established, many mutants found in patients are not yet classified or classified as Variants of Uncertain Significance. For newly discovered rare mutants, strong evidence supporting their classification into oncogenic
papers.summary: This study combines molecular dynamics simulations with machine learning to predict whether EGFR mutations found in lung cancer patients are oncogenic. The approach aims to help classify variants of uncertain significance, which could guide treatment decisions for non-small cell lung cancer. It offers a computational framework for prioritizing rare EGFR mutants for further experimental validation.

papers.title: Machine Learning Guided Discovery of Microbiome Metabolites That Inhibit HDAC.
papers.abstract: Histone deacetylase (HDAC) is a family of key epigenetic regulator implicated in inflammation, metabolism, and cancer. Microbiome metabolites can modulate host histone acetylation, yet systematic identification of metabolites that target HDAC remains limited. Here we present a computationally driven discovery pipeline that combines training data composition optimization with experimental validation to prioritize microbiome-derived HDAC inhibitors. Starting from a large, public HDAC3 screening data set (314,129 compounds; 485 actives), we developed an automated iterative sampling strategy that
papers.summary: This study presents a machine learning pipeline that screens microbiome-derived metabolites for their ability to inhibit histone deacetylase (HDAC), an epigenetic regulator linked to inflammation, metabolism, and cancer. Using a large public HDAC3 screening dataset of over 314,000 compounds, the authors developed an iterative sampling strategy to prioritize candidate microbiome metabolites and validated their predictions experimentally. The work demonstrates a computationally guided approach to discovering microbiome metabolites with epigenetic-modulating activity.

papers.title: Functional Annotation of Alzheimer's Disease-Associated SNPs Based on Three-Dimensional Chromatin Structure.
papers.abstract: Genome-wide association studies (GWASs) have identified numerous loci associated with Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet the effector genes and regulatory mechanisms underlying many of these associations remain unresolved. This challenge is particularly pronounced for non-coding variants, whose regulatory effects may extend over long genomic distances and cannot be reliably inferred from the nearest gene alone. Here, we developed an integrative computational framework that incorporates three-dimensional chromatin interactions, expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL), and sequence-level regulatory
papers.summary: This study presents a computational framework that integrates 3D chromatin interaction data, eQTL information, and sequence-level regulatory annotations to functionally annotate non-coding Alzheimer's disease-associated GWAS variants. By accounting for long-range regulatory contacts rather than simply assigning variants to the nearest gene, the approach aims to identify effector genes and regulatory mechanisms underlying AD risk loci. The work addresses a key bottleneck in translating GWAS findings into biological insight for non-coding variants.

papers.title: Integrative Proteomics and Genome-Scale Modeling Elucidate Metabolic Flux Shifts in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii CC-4414 Under Light Stress.
papers.abstract: The green microalga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii holds substantial promise as a photosynthetic cell factory for sustainable bioproduction, yet strain-specific metabolic responses to environmental stress remain underexplored. Here, we reconstructed a genome-scale metabolic network (GSMN) of the light-tolerant strain C. reinhardtii CC-4414 by combining de novo genome assembly with integrative proteomics. The resulting model, designated iYH2021, comprises 2021 genes, 2601 reactions, and 2089 metabolites, representing the first genome-scale metabolic reconstruction reported for this strain. To elucid
papers.summary: This study reconstructed the first genome-scale metabolic network for the light-tolerant Chlamydomonas reinhardtii strain CC-4414, combining de novo genome assembly with proteomics data. The resulting model, iYH2021, was used to analyze metabolic flux shifts under light stress, revealing strain-specific metabolic responses. This provides a new resource for understanding and engineering this microalga for bioproduction.

papers.title: Allele-Specific MicroRNA-Binding Variants at Colorectal Cancer Risk Loci in a Hispanic/Latino Population: An Integrative GWAS, All of Us, and Epigenomic Analysis.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) disproportionately affects Hispanic individuals, who remain underrepresented in genomic discovery and lack ancestry-matched functional resources. Many CRC risk variants are non-coding, and those in 3' untranslated regions (3' UTRs) can alter microRNA (miRNA) binding sites and reprogram post-transcriptional gene regulation. Here, we identify allele-specific miRNA-binding variants at CRC risk loci within the Hispanic population using a discovery pipeline anchored to Hispanic-relevant resources. CRC-associated 3' UTR variants were compiled from the GWAS Catalog, further ve
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This study identifies allele-specific microRNA-binding variants at colorectal cancer risk loci specifically in Hispanic/Latino populations by integrating GWAS data, the All of Us cohort, and epigenomic annotations. The work addresses the underrepresentation of Hispanic individuals in genomic research and highlights how non-coding 3' UTR variants may alter post-transcriptional gene regulation relevant to CRC risk.

papers.title: SMORE: joint dimension reduction and cell population discovery on single-cell methylome data.
papers.abstract: Single-cell DNA methylation profiling technology captures novel epigenetic data modality but are challenging to analyze because of their heterogeneity, high dimensionality, and ultra-sparsity. Here we present SMORE (Single-cell MethylOme Reduction and Embedding), a computational method for joint dimensionality reduction and cell population discovery dedicated to single cell DNA methylation data. SMORE operates on a Bayesian framework that converts methylation proportions into ordered methylation states and jointly infers a low-dimensional representation, cell populations and their number. By u
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: SMORE is a new computational method for analyzing single-cell DNA methylation data, which is extremely sparse and high-dimensional. It uses a Bayesian framework to simultaneously reduce dimensionality, discover cell populations, and determine the number of populations without requiring pre-specification. This addresses a key bottleneck in the emerging field of single-cell epigenomics.

papers.title: Exploring the association between gastroesophageal reflux disease and hyperlipidemia through bioinformatics and Mendelian randomization.
papers.abstract: Observational research has found a relationship between gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and hyperlipidemia (HLP). This study explored the relationship between GERD and HLP using bioinformatics and Mendelian randomization (MR) methods. We first conducted bioinformatics analyses to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs) from disease datasets and then performed a two-sample MR analysis with aggregated genome-wide association study (GWAS) data to investigate the relationship. 11 DEGs were shared between GERD and HLP. According to the Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) en
papers.summary: This study combined bioinformatics analyses of gene expression datasets with two-sample Mendelian randomization using GWAS summary statistics to investigate whether gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) is causally linked to hyperlipidemia (HLP). The authors identified 11 shared differentially expressed genes between the two conditions and used genetic instruments to assess a potential causal relationship. The work suggests a shared molecular basis and possible causal link between GERD and hyperlipidemia.

papers.title: HisTrader identifies nucleosome-free regions within ChIP-based profiling of histone post-translational modifications.
papers.abstract: Enhancers and promoters regulate cell identity through the binding of transcription factors (TFs) to specific DNA motifs within accessible chromatin. These regulatory regions are often identified using chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP)-based assays targeting histone modifications, such as ChIP sequencing (ChIP-seq), HiChIP, and proximity-ligation-assisted ChIP-seq (PLAC-seq). However, the large size of the enriched regions, or peaks, can make it difficult to pinpoint the precise DNA sequence where TFs act or where trait- or disease-associated variants exert their effects. We present HisTrad
papers.summary: HisTrader is a computational method that identifies nucleosome-free regions (NFRs) from ChIP-based profiling of histone post-translational modifications, such as ChIP-seq, HiChIP, and PLAC-seq. By pinpointing these accessible regions within broad histone modification peaks, it enables more precise localization of transcription factor binding sites and trait- or disease-associated variants.

papers.title: Using Brain Organoids to Explore Human Neurobiology.
papers.abstract: One of the major challenges in neuroscience is understanding how the human brain develops into a highly organized and functionally integrated organ, because many developmental processes cannot be investigated directly in humans and are not fully recapitulated in animal models. Brain organoids derived from human pluripotent stem cells have emerged as powerful three-dimensional (3D) experimental models that recapitulate key features of human neurodevelopment, including regional patterning, cellular diversification, and neural circuit assembly. Recent advances in long-term organoid culture, organ
papers.summary: This review discusses how brain organoids derived from human pluripotent stem cells serve as 3D models that recapitulate key features of human neurodevelopment, such as regional patterning and neural circuit assembly. It highlights recent advances in long-term culture that make these models increasingly useful for studying human neurobiology where animal models and direct human studies fall short.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Pediatric Cardiovascular Genetics: From Multimodal Diagnosis to Risk Prediction and Precision Therapeutics.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being explored as a bridge between high-dimensional cardiovascular phenotyping and genomic interpretation in children with inherited and congenital heart disease. This review focuses specifically on where AI-assisted approaches in pediatric cardiovascular genetics have progressed beyond proof-of-concept, how the maturity of evidence differs between general genomic tools and pediatric cardiovascular applications, and what is required for responsible clinical translation. Inherited and rare cardiovascular disorders are characterized by genetic heterog
papers.summary: This review examines how artificial intelligence is being used to connect detailed cardiovascular imaging and clinical data with genomic information in children with inherited and congenital heart disease. It highlights where AI approaches have moved past early proof-of-concept stages, contrasts the maturity of general genomic tools with pediatric cardiovascular applications, and outlines what is needed for responsible clinical translation.

papers.title: Beyond the drug-centric view: Advancing AI virtual cell platforms for environmental perturbation modelling.
papers.abstract: Environmental exposures contribute substantially to global morbidity and mortality, with their biological effects shaped by factors such as dose, exposure duration, life-stage timing, and cumulative or sequential exposure patterns. With rapid advances in AI based virtual cell (VC) technologies, current frameworks emphasize genet-ic and pharmacological perturbations, leaving environmental perturbations insufficiently modelled. This imbal-ance is due to fundamental structural limitations in data availability, chemical space coverage, and representa-tional design, as well as lacking standardized
papers.summary: This perspective argues that current AI virtual cell platforms are heavily focused on genetic and pharmacological perturbations, leaving environmental exposures inadequately modelled. The authors identify structural barriers—limited data, incomplete chemical space coverage, and representational design gaps—and call for standardized frameworks to advance environmental perturbation modelling.

papers.title: "Updates on diagnostic and prognostic molecular biomarkers of CNS tumors".
papers.abstract: The diagnosis and classification of central nervous system (CNS) tumors has undergone a paradigm shift over the past decade, evolving from a purely histology-based approach to an integrated framework that incorporates molecular and epigenetic features. This review summarizes recent updates in key genomic and epigenomic biomarkers across major CNS tumor categories, with a focus on their diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic implications. DNA methylation profiling has emerged as a valuable tool for tumor classification, subgrouping, and grading, complementing traditional histopathologic assess
papers.journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
papers.summary: This review summarizes recent advances in molecular and epigenetic biomarkers used to diagnose and classify central nervous system tumors, highlighting the shift from purely histology-based diagnosis to an integrated molecular framework. It emphasizes DNA methylation profiling as a key tool for tumor classification, subgrouping, and grading, alongside other genomic biomarkers with diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic relevance.

papers.title: Transcriptome-based epigenetic screening identifies DNA hypermethylation signatures as prognostic biomarkers in oral squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Promoter DNA hypermethylation is a key epigenetic mechanism of gene silencing in cancer, yet the DNA hypermethylome of oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) and its prognostic relevance remain poorly characterized. Here, we systematically identified and validated novel hypermethylated genes with prognostic significance in OSCC using a genome-wide discovery and multi-platform validation strategy. Candidate genes were first identified by pharmacologic demethylation combined with RNA sequencing across OSCC cell lines, then validated by quantitative RT-PCR, methylation-specific PCR, and bisulfite se
papers.summary: This study used pharmacological demethylation combined with RNA sequencing to identify genes silenced by promoter DNA hypermethylation in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) cell lines. Multi-platform validation confirmed novel hypermethylated genes with prognostic significance, suggesting DNA methylation signatures could serve as biomarkers for OSCC.

papers.title: Phage Genomics and Bioinformatics in Therapeutic Development: Evidence Limits, Validation Gates, and Translational Decision-Making.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Antimicrobial resistance has renewed interest in live therapeutic phages, including engineered candidates and defined phage cocktails, as antibacterial strategies. However, clinical translation requires evidence extending beyond phage isolation and computational prediction. This review examines how phage genomics and bioinformatics can support phage-based antibacterial development while remaining aligned with pharmaceutical requirements for safety, quality, pharmacology, and clinical validation. Methods: This narrative review synthesizes the literature on the generation,
papers.summary: This review examines how phage genomics and bioinformatics can support the development of phage-based antibacterial therapeutics, emphasizing that computational predictions and phage isolation alone are insufficient for clinical translation. It outlines evidence limits, validation gates, and decision-making frameworks needed to meet pharmaceutical standards for safety, quality, pharmacology, and clinical validation.

papers.title: The Plant Cell Wall: From Structural Diversity and Biosynthesis to Integrity Signaling and Physiological Functions.
papers.abstract: Plant cell walls are dynamic structural matrices that provide mechanical support while regulating growth, transport, environmental sensing, and defense. Their properties emerge from the coordinated biosynthesis, deposition, assembly, and remodeling of cellulose, hemicelluloses, pectins, lignin, and specialized wall polymers, yet how wall architecture is coupled to integrity surveillance and whole-plant physiology remains incompletely understood. Here, we synthesize current knowledge of plant cell wall classification, major polymer biosynthesis and assembly, cell wall integrity signaling, and p
papers.summary: This review synthesizes current knowledge on plant cell walls, covering their structural diversity, the biosynthesis and assembly of major polymers like cellulose, hemicellulose, pectin, and lignin, and how cell wall integrity signaling connects wall architecture to whole-plant physiology. It highlights that while the components are well characterized, how wall structure is coupled to integrity surveillance and broader physiological functions remains incompletely understood.

papers.title: FetchPA: a guided, end-to-end solution for local ATAC-Seq data processing and analyses.
papers.abstract: Local genome accessibility strongly correlates with activity of cis-regulatory elements, and Assay for Transposase-Accessible Chromatin coupled with next-generation sequencing (ATAC-Seq) has emerged as method of choice to profile chromatin accessibility in both healthy and pathogenic conditions. The introduction of streamlined protocols and manufacturer kits has made this technique accessible to labs of a variety of disciplines, background, and research interests. Many bioinformatics tools have been created for the quality control, mapping, and visualization of ATAC-seq data, however these too
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: FetchPA is a guided, end-to-end software solution that streamlines local processing and analysis of ATAC-Seq data, from quality control and read mapping through visualization. It aims to make chromatin accessibility profiling accessible to labs without extensive bioinformatics expertise by integrating existing tools into a single user-friendly workflow.

papers.title: Protocol for telomere-to-telomere assembly of Borrelia genomes using a hybrid method.
papers.abstract: Borrelia has a linear chromosome and linear plasmids capped by hairpin telomeres that short-read sequencing cannot resolve. Here, we present a protocol for telomere-to-telomere assembly of Borrelia genomes. We describe steps for spanning B. burgdorferi culture, DNA extraction, and sequencing through hybrid genome assembly to generate complete Borrelia genomes. The pipeline integrates Oxford Nanopore long reads and Illumina short reads to assemble hairpin telomeres, resolve paralogous linear and circular plasmids, and annotate and validate the assembled complete Borrelia genome. For complete de
papers.summary: This protocol describes a hybrid sequencing and assembly approach to generate complete, telomere-to-telomere Borrelia genomes, which are challenging due to their linear chromosomes and plasmids with hairpin telomeres. It combines Oxford Nanopore long reads with Illumina short reads to resolve telomeres and distinguish paralogous linear and circular plasmids, followed by annotation and validation. The workflow provides a step-by-step guide for producing fully finished Borrelia genomes.

papers.title: MACS3: A Peak-calling Platform for Bulk and Single-cell Regulatory Genomics.
papers.abstract: Since the original publication of Model-based Analysis for ChIP-Seq (MACS), the software has been widely used to identify enriched genomic regions in ChIP-seq, ATAC-seq, CUT&RUN, DNase-seq, and related regulatory genomics assays. Over the years, MACS has evolved substantially, with MACS version 3 (MACS3) now serving as the actively maintained implementation. MACS3 preserves the core MACS framework for fragment pileup, dynamic local background noise, statistical enrichment testing, and peak refinement, while adding functionality needed for contemporary bulk and single-cell workflows. It support
papers.summary: MACS3 is the actively maintained successor to the widely used MACS peak-calling software, preserving its core statistical framework for detecting enriched genomic regions while adding new capabilities for modern bulk and single-cell regulatory genomics assays like ChIP-seq, ATAC-seq, and CUT&RUN. It extends the tool to support single-cell workflows, making it a versatile platform for peak detection across a broad range of epigenomic experiments.

papers.title: The Epigenetic Aging-Cancer Continuum: Biomarkers, Metabolism, and Therapy.
papers.abstract: Aging and cancer form a biological continuum influenced by epigenomic changes, metabolic dysfunction, inflammation, cellular senescence, and loss of tissue homeostasis. Age-related epigenetic alterations can promote cancer, which exploits plasticity for evolution, immune evasion, metastasis, and resistance. Nutrition and metabolism affect this process through one-carbon metabolism, methyl-donor availability, acetyl-CoA and NAD+ balance, redox status, microbiome metabolites, and chromatin enzyme activity. Circulating biomarkers such as cell-free DNA methylation, mutation-based ctDNA, fragmentom
papers.summary: This review argues that aging and cancer are not separate processes but a biological continuum driven by epigenetic changes, metabolic dysfunction, inflammation, and cellular senescence. It highlights how nutrition and metabolism influence cancer through one-carbon metabolism, methyl donors, acetyl-CoA/NAD+ balance, and microbiome metabolites, and discusses circulating biomarkers like cell-free DNA methylation and ctDNA for tracking this continuum.

papers.title: A comprehensive map of the bovine mobilome and their epigenetic regulation of mastitis.
papers.abstract: Retrotransposons are major components of mammalian genomes, yet their genome-wide annotation and epigenetic regulation in cattle remain incompletely characterized. Here, we present a comprehensive annotation and integrative epigenomic analysis of major retrotransposon classes in the bovine genome, with emphasis on DNA methylation patterns and their potential roles in subclinical mastitis. Using a multi-step de novo pipeline, we identified and classified long interspersed nuclear elements (LINEs), short interspersed nuclear elements (SINEs), and endogenous retroviruses (ERVs) in the bovine refe
papers.summary: This study provides a comprehensive annotation of retrotransposons (LINEs, SINEs, and ERVs) in the bovine genome using a de novo pipeline, and integrates epigenomic data to examine DNA methylation patterns. It highlights potential links between retrotransposon epigenetic regulation and subclinical mastitis in cattle, offering a resource for understanding how mobile elements influence immune-related traits.

papers.title: Genome-Wide Identification and Characterization of the CBL Gene Family in Ziziphus jujuba var. spinosa.
papers.abstract: Calcineurin B-like (CBL) protein-mediated calcium signaling represents a core regulatory pathway underlying plant abiotic stress adaptation. Ziziphus jujuba var. spinosa (sour jujube) is a perennial woody species with remarkable saline-alkali and drought tolerance, yet the CBL gene family in this species has not been systematically characterized.
papers.summary: This study systematically identifies and characterizes the CBL (calcineurin B-like) gene family in sour jujube, a woody species known for its tolerance to saline-alkali and drought conditions. The authors provide a genome-wide catalog of these calcium-signaling genes, laying groundwork for understanding how this species adapts to abiotic stress.

papers.title: Genetic Variants Involved in Metformin Pharmacokinetics in the Chilean Population.
papers.abstract: To estimate the frequency and potential impact of genetic variants involved in metformin pharmacokinetics, including gastrointestinal absorption, renal elimination, and hepatic transport in the Chilean population.
papers.summary: This study estimates the frequency of genetic variants affecting metformin pharmacokinetics—covering gastrointestinal absorption, renal elimination, and hepatic transport—in the Chilean population. It aims to assess how these variant frequencies might influence metformin response and dosing in this understudied population. The work contributes population-specific pharmacogenomic data relevant to diabetes treatment.

papers.title: The Exposome-Brain Axis: A Scoping Review of Biological Biomarkers in Environmental Neurotoxicity, Neuroinflammation, and Neurodegeneration.
papers.abstract: The escalating global burden of neurodegenerative and neuropsychiatric disorders is deeply intertwined with cumulative environmental toxicant exposure. To accurately capture the prodromal and subclinical impacts of this multi-chemical "pollutome", research is shifting from symptom-based assessments toward the use of objective, quantifiable biological indicators. Guided by the PRISMA-ScR framework, this scoping review systematically analyzed literature across PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase databases without temporal restrictions. The final selection included 52 human observational s
papers.summary: This scoping review synthesizes 52 human observational studies examining biological biomarkers that link environmental toxicant exposure (the 'exposome') to neurotoxicity, neuroinflammation, and neurodegeneration. It highlights a shift from symptom-based assessments toward objective, quantifiable biomarkers for capturing prodromal and subclinical neurological impacts of cumulative chemical exposures.

papers.title: H3K27me3 Drives Constricted Migration-Induced 3D Genome Rewiring in Melanoma.
papers.abstract: Repeated exposure of neoplastic cells to mechanical stresses during metastasis can drive stable morphological and physiological changes. We previously showed that A375 human melanoma cells subjected to 10 rounds of constricted migration ("Bottom-10 cells") became significantly more migratory and exhibited H3K9me3 relocalization, transcriptional remodeling, and chromatin compartment changes relative to naïve parental A375 cells. Because these phenotypes persist across cell divisions, we hypothesized they are driven and maintained by specific epigenetic mechanisms. We profiled candidate histone
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study investigates how repeated mechanical stress from constricted migration alters the 3D genome organization of melanoma cells. The authors find that H3K27me3, a repressive histone modification, drives and maintains these chromatin rewiring changes, which persist across cell divisions and may promote metastatic behavior.

papers.title: Deep Learning-Assisted Prioritization of Candidate Drug Targets in Tumors Using Spatial Multi-Omics.
papers.abstract: Tumor heterogeneity is reflected in cell composition, molecular states, spatial distribution, and microenvironment interactions. Spatial transcriptomics can map in situ expression and cell states but cannot fully explain upstream regulation, while spatial epigenomics provides complementary evidence such as chromatin accessibility, histone modifications, and deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) methylation. This review summarizes the applications of spatial multi-omics and deep learning in prioritizing candidate drug targets in tumors.
papers.summary: This review discusses how spatial multi-omics technologies (combining spatial transcriptomics and spatial epigenomics) can be integrated with deep learning to identify and prioritize candidate drug targets in tumors. It highlights that spatial transcriptomics alone cannot capture upstream regulatory mechanisms, but adding spatial epigenomic data provides complementary evidence such as chromatin accessibility and DNA methylation. The review summarizes current applications and approaches in this emerging intersection of spatial biology, deep learning, and oncology drug discovery.

papers.title: Disentangling covariate effects on single-cell-resolved epigenomes with DeepDive.
papers.abstract: Understanding the effects of individual biological factors from single-cell-resolved epigenomic data is hindered by multicollinearity, particularly in human cohorts. We introduce DeepDive, a deep-learning framework designed to systematically disentangle known and unknown sources of variation in single-nucleus ATAC-seq data. DeepDive accurately reconstructs chromatin accessibility, outperforms state-of-the-art methods with incomplete covariate information, and robustly recovers true biological signals from even highly entangled covariates, unlocking counterfactual, "what-if," analyses. Applying
papers.summary: DeepDive is a deep-learning framework that disentangles the effects of individual biological factors from single-nucleus ATAC-seq data, addressing the problem of multicollinearity in human cohort studies. It accurately reconstructs chromatin accessibility and outperforms existing methods when covariate information is incomplete, enabling counterfactual 'what-if' analyses of epigenomic variation.

papers.title: Complete Mitochondrial Genome of the Endemic Loach Leptobotia tchangi and Its Phylogenetic Placement Within Botiidae.
papers.abstract: Leptobotia tchangi is a loach species endemic to South China, but its mitochondrial genome has not yet been characterized, limiting understanding of its evolutionary relationships and conservation genetics.
papers.summary: This study reports the first complete mitochondrial genome of Leptobotia tchangi, a loach endemic to South China, and uses it to infer the species' phylogenetic position within the family Botiidae. The mitogenome provides a new genomic resource for evolutionary and conservation studies of this endemic fish.

papers.title: Recurrent mechanisms of biallelic epigenetic inactivation reveal new putative tumour suppressor genes in prostate cancer.
papers.abstract: The inactivation of tumour suppressor genes is a key step in cancer development, and is usually achieved by homozygous loss. In prostate cancer, however, large genomic regions are often hemizygously lost, which complicates the identification of putative tumour suppressors in these regions. Here, we develop Epi2Hit, an integrative computational method that leverages whole genome sequencing, epigenomic profiling and gene expression to identify biallelic inactivation of tumour suppressor genes involving DNA methylation of promoter and enhancer regions of one allele and genomic loss of the other a
papers.summary: The authors developed Epi2Hit, a computational method that integrates whole-genome sequencing, epigenomic profiling, and gene expression data to detect biallelic inactivation of tumour suppressor genes caused by DNA methylation of one allele combined with genomic loss of the other. Applying this to prostate cancer, they identified recurrent epigenetic silencing events and nominated new putative tumour suppressor genes that would be missed by approaches focused only on homozygous deletion.

papers.title: A patient-derived missense mouse model of Kabuki syndrome 1.
papers.abstract: Kabuki syndrome type 1 (KS1) is a rare cause of intellectual disability resulting from heterozygous pathogenic variants in the gene encoding the histone methyltransferase KMT2D. A previously established loss-of-function mouse model of KS1 exhibits key phenotypic features, and therapeutic trials in this mouse model suggest postnatal malleability of neurological symptoms. However, 15-30% of individuals with KS1 carry missense variants. To investigate whether missense variants lead to similar phenotypic presentation in mice, we used CRISPR-Cas9 to introduce the KS1- patient variant R5179, corresp
papers.summary: This study uses CRISPR-Cas9 to create a mouse model carrying a patient-derived missense variant (R5179) in KMT2D, the gene mutated in Kabuki syndrome type 1. The model allows researchers to study whether missense mutations produce similar phenotypes to the previously characterized loss-of-function models, which is important since 15-30% of KS1 patients have missense variants.

papers.title: Multiscale Modeling Primer: Focus on Chromatin and Epigenetics.
papers.abstract: A central challenge in modern biology is to understand how molecular interactions produce cellular and organismal functions across vast spatiotemporal scales. Nowhere is this challenge more apparent than in the study of chromatin, where meters of DNA compact into a micron-sized nucleus. How this polymer folds is a dynamic process, regulated by epigenetic modifications-chemical changes to DNA and histones that involve only a handful of atoms. These small changes cooperate to produce emergent, higher-order structures that define cellular identity and function. To explain this system, we must int
papers.summary: This primer reviews multiscale modeling approaches for understanding how chromatin folds within the nucleus and how epigenetic modifications—small chemical changes to DNA and histones—give rise to higher-order chromatin structures that define cellular identity. It emphasizes the challenge of connecting molecular-scale interactions to emergent cellular and organismal functions across vast spatiotemporal scales.

papers.title: Programmable RNA-Guided DNA Recombination: Mechanisms, Engineering, and Applications.
papers.abstract: The emergence of seekRNA- and bridgeRNA-guided recombination has introduced a distinct paradigm in genome engineering by coupling programmable RNA-directed DNA recognition with recombinase-mediated insertion, excision, inversion, and genomic rearrangement without canonical double-strand breaks. Since their discovery in 2024, these systems have progressed rapidly from bacterial mobile genetic elements and mechanistic characterization to structural elucidation and programmable genome engineering in human cells. However, these advances remain distributed across foundational and rapidly emerging s
papers.summary: This review covers seekRNA- and bridgeRNA-guided DNA recombination systems, which use programmable RNA to direct recombinases for DNA insertion, excision, and inversion without creating double-strand breaks. It traces their rapid development since 2024 from bacterial mobile elements to structural understanding and engineering in human cells, while noting that the field's advances remain scattered across foundational and emerging studies.

papers.title: Cross-Scale Convergence in Epigenetic Gene Regulation: A Perspective on Functional Enrichment Analytics for Cancer.
papers.abstract: Epigenetic regulation of gene expression is studied at three physical scales: micro: DNA sequence-level methylation/demethylation; meso: nucleosome occupancy and remodeling; and macro: chromosomal domain silencing by Polycomb complexes, heterochromatin, and topologically associating domain (TAD) boundaries. The challenge to fully understand epigenetic gene regulation patterns is that these scales are not independent. Their influence overlaps and they share a recurring architectural theme across scales of a targeted molecular pattern followed by cooperative, feedback-driven, spatially bounded s
papers.summary: This perspective argues that epigenetic gene regulation operates across three interconnected physical scales—DNA methylation (micro), nucleosome remodeling (meso), and higher-order chromatin domains like TADs and Polycomb silencing (macro)—and that these scales share a recurring architectural motif of targeted molecular patterning followed by cooperative, feedback-driven spatial confinement. The authors propose that functional enrichment analytics must account for this cross-scale convergence to properly interpret epigenetic patterns in cancer.

papers.title: GenoME: a MoE-based generative model for individualized, multimodal prediction and perturbation of genomic profiles.
papers.abstract: The non-coding genome operates through a complex, multiscale regulatory system where regulated gene expressions are closely associated with cell-type-specific histone modifications, transcription factor binding, and 3D conformation. Developing computational models that can integrate these patterns to predict and interpret the regulatory system remains challenging. Here, we present GenoME, a Mixture of Experts (MoE)-based generative model that uses DNA sequence and cell-type-specific ATAC-seq signals to predict a unified genomic profiles encompassing epigenomics, transcriptomics, and chromatin
papers.summary: GenoME is a Mixture-of-Experts generative model that integrates DNA sequence and cell-type-specific ATAC-seq signals to predict multimodal genomic profiles spanning epigenomics, transcriptomics, and chromatin conformation. It enables individualized, multimodal prediction and in silico perturbation of regulatory profiles, offering a unified framework for interpreting the non-coding regulatory system.

papers.title: DNA methylation-based ageing in a deuterostome invertebrate: an epigenetic clock for the crown-of-thorns seastar (Acanthaster cf. solaris).
papers.abstract: Accurate and reliable ageing tools are essential for wildlife conservation and management. While DNA methylation has emerged as a promising tool for age estimation in vertebrates, its application to invertebrates remains contested and has been limited to arthropods. Here, we develop an epigenetic clock for the Pacific crown-of-thorns seastar (CoTS; Acanthaster cf. solaris), a destructive coral predator contributing to habitat degradation across Indo-Pacific reefs. Using Oxford Nanopore Technologies, we generated whole-genome DNA methylation profiles across five age groups and identified 1910 C
papers.summary: This study developed the first DNA methylation-based epigenetic clock for an echinoderm, the crown-of-thorns seastar, using Oxford Nanopore whole-genome methylation profiling across five age groups. The clock identifies 1910 age-associated CpG sites and demonstrates that epigenetic ageing tools can work in non-arthropod invertebrates, extending their applicability beyond vertebrates and insects.

papers.title: A Marine Brevibacillus-Derived Membrane-Lytic Peptide: Molecular Insight and Biophysical Characterization of a Novel AMP, FNL62-AMP.
papers.abstract: This study characterizes the genomic identity, functional efficacy, and computational biophysics of FNL62-AMP, a novel antimicrobial peptide isolated from a phylogenomically distinct, newly identified Brevibacillus species. Production kinetics revealed a late-exponential phase onset of antibacterial activity with sustained potency against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). LC-MS/MS analysis identified the peptide sequence as NH2-LLLLFR-COOH. FNL62-AMP demonstrated excellent formulation resilience, retaining full anti-MRSA activity under high thermal stress (80 °C for 6 h) and
papers.summary: This study identifies and characterizes FNL62-AMP, a novel antimicrobial peptide from a newly identified marine Brevibacillus species, with the sequence LLLLFR. The peptide shows sustained activity against MRSA and remains fully active after extreme heat stress (80 °C for 6 hours), suggesting promise as a stable anti-infective candidate.

papers.title: Classical Homocystinuria Incidentally Diagnosed Following a Normal Newborn Screening Result.
papers.abstract: Classical homocystinuria (HCY) due to cystathionine beta-synthase (CBS) deficiency is included in many newborn screening programs, which traditionally use dried blood spot (DBS) methionine as the primary biomarker. However, some patients have normal or only mildly elevated methionine in the neonatal period, leading to false-negative results. We report a four-month-old male infant referred for sagittal craniosynostosis, whose metabolic evaluation revealed markedly elevated plasma methionine and total homocysteine concentrations. Genetic analysis identified a homozygous, pathogenic variant (c.10
papers.summary: This case report describes a four-month-old infant with classical homocystinuria who had a normal newborn screening result, highlighting a false-negative due to normal or only mildly elevated methionine levels in the neonatal period. The diagnosis was made incidentally after referral for sagittal craniosynostosis, when metabolic testing revealed markedly elevated plasma methionine and total homocysteine, and genetic testing confirmed a homozygous pathogenic CBS variant.

papers.title: Co-Directional Chromosomal Clustering of Metabolic Pathway Genes as a Layout Prior for Synthetic Construct Design.
papers.abstract: Metabolic pathway design tools largely address reaction routes and enzyme choice, whereas a complementary set of questions-how pathway genes are arranged on bacterial chromosomes and whether co-directional neighborhoods can inform multi-gene construct layout-has received comparatively little systematic treatment. Here, we present SynPAL (Synteny-Informed Pathway Assembly and Layout), a computational analysis that scores co-directional clustering of BioCyc pathway genes from genomic coordinates (same replicon and strand, intergenic distance ≤ 2000 bp) and translates the resulting scores into de
papers.summary: The authors introduce SynPAL, a computational tool that scores how frequently genes within metabolic pathways are clustered co-directionally on bacterial chromosomes. These synteny-based scores are then used as a prior to guide the layout of multi-gene synthetic constructs, aiming to improve pathway assembly design.

papers.title: Cross-Model Uncertainty-Aware Minimal Editing of Cis-Regulatory Elements for Cell-Type-Selective Design.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Cis-regulatory elements (CREs) help mediate cell-type-selective gene expression, yet sequence-to-activity models are rarely converted into compact, experimentally tractable variant panels that retain natural regulatory scaffolds. We developed SafeEdit-CRE to select minimal edits that preserve cross-model specificity while reducing predictive uncertainty, yielding an auditable CRE variant library for reporter-screening prioritization. Methods: SafeEdit-CRE combines the published Malinois sequence-activity predictor with an architecture-distinct reviewer ensemble, validati
papers.summary: SafeEdit-CRE is a computational framework that designs minimal edits to cis-regulatory elements (CREs) to achieve cell-type-selective gene expression while preserving the natural regulatory scaffold. It combines the Malinois sequence-to-activity model with an independent reviewer ensemble to reduce predictive uncertainty and produce a compact, auditable variant library for reporter-screening experiments.

papers.title: Whole mitogenome profile of Pelung and Sentul chickens to reveal potency of Indonesian livestock genetic resources.
papers.abstract: Native chickens are essential genetic resources in Indonesia, providing economic, cultural, and nutritional value with strong adaptability to local environments. Among these native chickens, Sentul and Pelung are recognized as national genetic resources due to dual-purpose and ornamental traits, respectively, but their whole mitogenome characterization remains limited. Therefore, this study aimed to assemble and analyze the whole mitogenome of Sentul and Pelung chickens as well as perform a comparison with 35 additional genomes from domestic chickens and jungle fowls across Asia. The experimen
papers.summary: This study assembled and analyzed the complete mitochondrial genomes of two Indonesian native chicken breeds, Sentul and Pelung, and compared them with 35 other domestic chicken and jungle fowl mitogenomes from across Asia. The analysis characterizes the genetic diversity and phylogenetic relationships of these breeds, supporting their recognition as distinct national genetic resources. The findings provide baseline genomic data useful for conservation and breeding programs.

papers.title: The bioinformatics approach to identifying pathogenic variants for colorectal cancer (CRC).
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is the third most prevalent cancer globally, accounting for 9.6% of newly diagnosed cases and 9.3% of cancer-related deaths. It develops from the uncontrolled proliferation of glandular cells in the colon and rectum and is categorized into three primary types: sporadic, hereditary, and colitis-associated. While genetic susceptibility is a key factor in CRC pathogenesis, identifying high-impact pathogenic variants remains a significant challenge. This study integrates bioinformatics and population genetics approaches to identify CRC-associated single-nucleotide polymorph
papers.summary: This study applies bioinformatics and population genetics methods to identify single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) associated with colorectal cancer, aiming to pinpoint high-impact pathogenic variants that contribute to disease susceptibility. It highlights the challenge of distinguishing functionally relevant variants from the many genetic changes observed in CRC and proposes an integrated computational pipeline to prioritize them.

papers.title: Unlocking cis-regulatory landscapes across 500 million years of evolution and disease mechanisms.
papers.abstract: Genomic DNA encodes regulatory information that determines where, when, and to what extent genes are expressed. Theoretically, we should be able to identify these transcriptional "instructions" by examining genomic DNA sequence alone, yet this has remained challenging. Here we present the Vertebrate Regulatory MOdule Detector (VRMOD), a method that accurately predicts gene regulatory sequences using only the query genomic sequences. We applied VRMOD to 309 Ensembl genomes, generating a compendium of high-resolution, genome-position-fixed cis-regulatory modules without parameter tuning. We perf
papers.summary: The authors present VRMOD, a method that predicts cis-regulatory modules directly from genomic sequence alone, without requiring parameter tuning or species-specific training data. Applying it to 309 Ensembl genomes, they generated a cross-species compendium of high-resolution regulatory elements spanning roughly 500 million years of vertebrate evolution. This resource enables comparative study of regulatory landscapes and their links to disease mechanisms.

papers.title: Nanopore metagenomic sequencing links clinically relevant resistance determinants to pathogens.
papers.abstract: Culture-independent metagenomics enables the detection of plasmid-encoded antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes directly from clinical samples; however, the clinical significance of these genes depends on their bacterial host and genomic context, which metagenomics cannot fully infer. Nanopore sequencing technology intrinsically encodes epigenetic modifications such as methylation, which can be leveraged for plasmid-host associations from metagenomic data. Existing methods rely on the recovery of metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs), which can introduce bias towards abundant taxa and leave clini
papers.summary: This study uses nanopore sequencing's native methylation signals to link plasmid-encoded antimicrobial resistance genes to their bacterial hosts directly from clinical metagenomic samples, bypassing the need for metagenome-assembled genomes. This approach improves the clinical interpretability of resistance gene detection by revealing which pathogens carry resistance determinants.

papers.title: metaKEGG: A comprehensive algorithm package to visualize multi-omics pathway enrichment.
papers.abstract: metaKEGG is a comprehensive software package designed to streamline the visualization and integration of pathway enrichment results from multi-omics data, providing accessible and detailed insights into the molecular mechanisms driving health and disease. Unlike standard pipeline approaches, metaKEGG incorporates novel concepts allowing for clear, granular representation of gene-level or transcript-level expression changes. Beyond transcriptomic analysis, metaKEGG also supports epigenetic and regulatory metadata layers, such as methylation profiles and miRNA target annotations, offering users
papers.summary: metaKEGG is a new software package that visualizes and integrates pathway enrichment results across multiple omics layers, including transcriptomic, epigenetic, and regulatory data. It introduces novel concepts for granular gene- or transcript-level representation of expression changes, going beyond standard pathway enrichment pipelines. The tool aims to provide accessible, detailed insights into molecular mechanisms underlying health and disease.

papers.title: Establishment of a Common Marmoset Lineage Carrying a Frameshift Mutation in SETD1A, a Schizophrenia Risk Gene.
papers.abstract: Appropriate histone modifications are essential for maintaining functional chromatin structure and gene expression, and dysfunction of their regulators has been linked to a variety of diseases. Among these modifications, trimethylation of lysine 4 on histone H3 (H3K4me3) is a well-characterized epigenetic mark enriched at transcription start sites of actively transcribed genes. H3K4me3 regulates gene transcription by recruiting transcription factors, facilitating chromatin accessibility, and preventing DNA methylation. In mammals, methylation of H3K4 is catalyzed by a family of histone methylt
papers.summary: This paper reports the establishment of a common marmoset lineage carrying a frameshift mutation in SETD1A, a histone methyltransferase gene and known schizophrenia risk gene. The mutation disrupts H3K4me3-mediated epigenetic regulation, providing a non-human primate model to study how this chromatin regulator contributes to schizophrenia-related neurodevelopmental phenotypes.

papers.title: DNAmBERT: a transformer-based model for non-invasive cancer diagnosis using DNA sequence and methylation data.
papers.abstract: DNA methylation alterations are early and stable hallmarks of cancer and represent promising biomarkers for non-invasive detection using circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA). However, current computational approaches often model DNA sequence and methylation features separately and struggle to capture complex read-level methylation architecture in heterogeneous, low-signal liquid biopsy data. Here, we present DNAmBERT, a Transformer-based deep learning framework designed to jointly model DNA sequence context and read-level methylation haplotype structure from cfDNA methylation sequencing data. DNA
papers.summary: DNAmBERT is a Transformer-based deep learning framework that jointly models DNA sequence context and read-level methylation haplotype structure from circulating cell-free DNA to enable non-invasive cancer diagnosis. Unlike prior approaches that treat sequence and methylation features separately, it captures complex read-level methylation architecture in low-signal liquid biopsy data.

papers.title: MethyAnno: An Interpretable Automated Annotation Method Leveraging Multi-Scale Information and Metric Learning Framework for scDNAm Data.
papers.abstract: Single-cell DNA methylation (scDNAm) sequencing provides unique insights into epigenetic heterogeneity and cell-specific regulatory landscapes. However, accurate cell type annotation for scDNAm data remains challenging, as the distinct data distribution of scDNAm hinders the adaptation of annotation methods from other omics, and specialized annotation tools for scDNAm are currently lacking. Here, MethyAnno is proposed as an interpretable deep metric learning framework that leverages multi-scale information for accurate cell type annotation of scDNAm data. Additionally, MethyAnno enables genera
papers.summary: MethyAnno is a new interpretable deep metric learning framework for automatically annotating cell types in single-cell DNA methylation (scDNAm) data, addressing the lack of specialized tools for this data type. It leverages multi-scale information to handle the distinct data distribution of scDNAm and provides interpretable results, enabling accurate cell type identification.

papers.title: Sotagliflozin, a Dual SGLT1/2 Inhibitor, Modulates DNMT1 and Class I/II HDAC Expression in Association With Anticancer Effects in Breast and Lung Cancer Cells.
papers.abstract: Sodium-glucose cotransporter (SGLT) inhibitors are increasingly recognised for anticancer activity beyond their established glycaemic effects. While selective SGLT2 inhibitors have been reported to suppress tumour cell proliferation and modulate AMPK/mTOR and PI3K/AKT signalling, whether dual SGLT1/2 inhibition is associated with modulation of epigenetic regulators has remained largely unexplored. Here, we investigated the anticancer effects of sotagliflozin, a dual SGLT1/2 inhibitor, in breast (MCF-7) and lung (A549) cancer cells. Sotagliflozin reduced cell viability, clonogenic survival, mig
papers.summary: Sotagliflozin, a dual SGLT1/2 inhibitor, reduced viability, clonogenic survival, and migration in breast (MCF-7) and lung (A549) cancer cells. The anticancer effects were accompanied by changes in expression of the epigenetic regulators DNMT1 and class I/II HDACs, suggesting a link between SGLT inhibition and epigenetic modulation.

papers.title: Epigenetic Insights in Pediatric Multiple Sclerosis: DNA Methylation Highlights an Involvement of Epstein-Barr Virus Infection and Host Immune Networks.
papers.abstract: Pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis (PedMS) provides a unique opportunity to investigate MS pathogenesis because of the short interval between environmental exposures and disease onset. This study aimed to identify differentially methylated regions (DMRs) that mediate the interplay between environmental triggers and genomic factors in the early stages of the disease.
papers.summary: This study analyzed DNA methylation patterns in pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis (PedMS) patients to identify differentially methylated regions linking environmental exposures to disease. The findings highlight the involvement of Epstein-Barr virus infection and host immune networks in early MS pathogenesis, leveraging the short exposure-to-onset interval unique to pediatric cases.

papers.title: ECHO: a nanopore sequencing-based workflow for (epi)genetic profiling of the human repeatome.
papers.abstract: The human genome is dominated by repetitive DNA, whose genetic and epigenetic variation plays a key role in gene regulation, genome stability, and disease. Recent advances in long-read sequencing now enable large-scale, haplotype-resolved, and DNA methylation-informative analysis of the human genome, including on previously inaccessible complex and repetitive regions. However, the comprehensive, simultaneous characterisation of the "human repeatome" remains challenging, largely due to the lack of comprehensive tools integrated in a single pipeline that can capture the full spectrum of variatio
papers.summary: ECHO is a new bioinformatics workflow that uses nanopore long-read sequencing to simultaneously profile genetic and epigenetic (methylation) variation across the human repeatome—the large, repetitive portions of the genome that are typically hard to analyze. It addresses the lack of integrated tools capable of capturing the full spectrum of repeat variation in a single pipeline.

papers.title: Association and Mechanistic Insights Linking Bisphenol A to Psoriasis: Integrative Analysis of Bulk Transcriptomics, Network Toxicology, Mendelian Randomization and Single‑cell RNA Sequencing.
papers.abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic immune-mediated skin disease with complex etiology, and environmental factors such as bisphenol A (BPA) exposure are suspected pathogenic factors. This study aimed to identify potential diagnostic biomarkers linking BPA exposure to psoriasis and to explore the latent interaction and mechanisms between BPA and candidate biomarkers.
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk transcriptomics, network toxicology, Mendelian randomization, and single-cell RNA sequencing to identify diagnostic biomarkers linking bisphenol A (BPA) exposure to psoriasis. The authors propose candidate genes and mechanistic pathways through which BPA may contribute to psoriasis pathogenesis, combining epidemiological causal inference with molecular profiling.

papers.title: Integrated genomic analysis of Stenotrophomonas maltophilia: resistome, virulence-associated genes, predicted mobile genetic elements, and core-genome phylogeny.
papers.abstract: Stenotrophomonas maltophilia is an emerging opportunistic pathogen characterized by intrinsic multidrug resistance and broad ecological distribution. However, its genomic characteristics across publicly available clinical, environmental, and animal isolates remain incompletely defined.
papers.summary: This study performs an integrated genomic analysis of Stenotrophomonas maltophilia isolates from clinical, environmental, and animal sources, characterizing their resistome, virulence-associated genes, and mobile genetic elements. It also reconstructs a core-genome phylogeny to clarify the evolutionary relationships among these isolates. The work provides a broader genomic picture of this emerging multidrug-resistant opportunistic pathogen across diverse niches.

papers.title: Residual based anomaly detection framework for variant caller dispatch in DNA sequencing data.
papers.abstract: Reliable and scalable variant analysis is an enabling component of genomic studies involving microbial communities, host-associated microorganisms, and their hosts, and may support future investigations of genetic heterogeneity within symbiotic systems. Widely used workflows incorporating BWA and GATK provide standardized default processing routes, but their performance may vary across genomic regions containing repetitive sequences, complex structures, or atypical local sequence characteristics. Applying a context-aware software-recommendation procedure to every genomic region, however, can s
papers.summary: This paper proposes a residual-based anomaly detection framework to decide which variant caller to use for different genomic regions in DNA sequencing data. The goal is to improve variant calling reliability in microbial and host-associated genomes where standard BWA/GATK workflows may underperform in repetitive or structurally complex regions. The approach aims to avoid the computational cost of applying context-aware recommendations to every region.

papers.title: Alzheimer's disease: genetic background in the era of next-generation sequencing technologies.
papers.abstract: While rare, highly penetrant variants in APP, PSEN1 and PSEN2 are associated with early-onset Alzheimer's disease, especially its familial form, the disease in general is shaped by a complex interplay of various genetic factors. Both common and rare variants across numerous loci, which were identified mainly during large genome-wide association studies, contribute to disease risk, phenotypic heterogeneity and progression in both early- and late-onset forms. This review synthesizes current understanding of the genetic architecture of Alzheimer's disease in the era of next-generation sequencing,
papers.summary: This review synthesizes current knowledge of Alzheimer's disease genetics, covering both rare, highly penetrant mutations in APP, PSEN1, and PSEN2 that cause early-onset familial forms, and the broader polygenic architecture of common and rare variants identified through genome-wide association studies. It emphasizes how next-generation sequencing technologies have expanded understanding of the complex genetic factors shaping disease risk, phenotypic heterogeneity, and progression across early- and late-onset forms.

papers.title: Potential Contribution of DES (p.Leu88Met) and MYH7 (p.Arg787His) Variants to Familial Restrictive Cardiomyopathy.
papers.abstract: Restrictive cardiomyopathy (RCM) is a rare, severe cardiac disease with a heterogeneous genetic basis. Both genetic and nongenetic factors contribute to RCM pathogenesis. Identifying the underlying molecular causes is important for diagnosis and family screening. In this study, we investigated the genetic basis of RCM in a 52-year-old woman with a family history of RCM and heart disease.
papers.summary: This case study reports a 52-year-old woman with familial restrictive cardiomyopathy (RCM) carrying two rare variants: DES p.Leu88Met and MYH7 p.Arg787His. The findings suggest these variants may contribute to RCM pathogenesis, though functional validation is lacking, highlighting the genetic heterogeneity of the disease.

papers.title: In silico transcriptomic analysis nominates TSPAN32 as a central node of SCFA-driven immunometabolic reprogramming in intestinal epithelial cells.
papers.abstract: Microbial short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) regulate intestinal epithelial homeostasis and immune tolerance. Yet, the specific host effector genes that mediate these responses remain poorly defined, limiting the identification of biomarkers and therapeutic targets.
papers.summary: This study uses computational (in silico) analysis of transcriptomic data to identify host genes that respond to microbial short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) in intestinal epithelial cells. The authors nominate TSPAN32 as a central hub gene in the SCFA-driven immunometabolic reprogramming network, suggesting it as a potential biomarker or therapeutic target. The work is purely computational and would require experimental validation to confirm its role.

papers.title: From sequence to timescale: a frequency-domain control-theoretic framework linking ncRNA sequence composition to epigenetic regulatory timescales.
papers.abstract: Non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) are central regulators of epigenomic states, orchestrating chromatin modifications, gene silencing, and nuclear architecture through recruitment of chromatin-modifying complexes. Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) such as XIST, HOTAIR, and MALAT1 exemplify these regulatory roles. Despite their importance, quantitative computational frameworks for linking ncRNA sequence composition to temporal regulatory behaviour remain limited. We introduce a frequency-domain control theory framework modelling RNA sequences as cascaded feedback systems, extending a previously established s
papers.summary: The authors propose a frequency-domain control theory framework that models non-coding RNA sequences as cascaded feedback systems, aiming to link sequence composition to the timescales of epigenetic regulation. This extends prior work by providing a quantitative computational approach to connect ncRNA sequence features with temporal regulatory dynamics.
